bug: SQL injection: req.query.orderId interpolated straight into the query

findings.message: `orderId` is taken directly from `req.query` and concatenated into the SQL string. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL here by supplying a crafted query parameter.
findings.suggestion: return db.query(`SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?`, [orderId]);

findings.message: `req.query.orderId` is used without validating that it exists and has the expected type/format. If the parameter is missing or non-numeric, this function may generate an invalid query or return an unintended result.

bug: Command injection: req.query.path passed unescaped into exec

findings.message: `req.query.path` is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to `exec()`, so an attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands via the `path` query parameter.

Using `exec()` here also invokes a shell and will mis-handle file paths with spaces or shell metacharacters even when the input is benign. This helper should invoke the binary without a shell and explicitly validate/escape the input path.

bug: Path traversal: req.query.file (e.g. ../../etc/passwd) read with no sanitization

findings.message: `req.query.file` is concatenated directly into a filesystem path, allowing path traversal (for example `../../etc/passwd`) and arbitrary file reads outside the uploads directory.
`readFileSync` blocks the Node.js event loop on every request. If avatar downloads are served in the request path, this can degrade throughput and stall unrelated requests under load.

bug: Off-by-one: loop uses <= length, reads items[length] (out of bounds / undefined)

findings.message: The loop condition uses `<= items.length`, so the final iteration reads `items[items.length]`, which is `undefined`. Accessing `.price` on that value will throw at runtime for any non-empty array and also adds an extra iteration for empty arrays.

bug: Assignment in condition: if (user.role = 'admin') assigns, always truthy -> auth bypass

findings.message: This condition uses assignment (`=`) instead of comparison, so it always evaluates truthy and also mutates `user.role` to `'admin'`. As written, every caller will be treated as an admin and the user's role is overwritten.

bug: Hardcoded live secret key committed in source

findings.message: A live Stripe secret key is hardcoded into the repository. This exposes production credentials to anyone with access to the code and makes rotation/revocation difficult.
The Stripe client is created without specifying an API version. That can cause behavior changes when the account default version changes and make responses inconsistent across deployments.
findings.suggestion: export const stripe = new Stripe(STRIPE_SECRET, { apiVersion: '2024-06-20' });

bug: Insecure randomness: Math.random() used to mint a security-sensitive reset token

findings.message: `Math.random()` is not suitable for generating password reset tokens. Its output is predictable enough that an attacker could potentially guess valid reset links, which would allow account takeover.

bug: Empty catch swallows the payment error; checkout reports success even when the charge failed

findings.message: `gateway.charge(...)` failures are swallowed, so the function returns success even when the payment is declined or the gateway throws. Callers will treat failed checkouts as completed.
`ok` is never updated, so `success` is always `true` regardless of the charge result. This makes the returned status unusable for callers.
